clue.text: Verse collection: Dante’s Inferno at beginning, trying to grapple with evil and ending in Paradiso?

indicators.note: Asks for each of the two words only at its beginning, its opening letter.
Things that grapple are twisted and tangled together, so the letters caught up in it are thrown out of order.

blocks.note: the opening letters of Dante’s and Inferno

blocks.clueFragment: trying to grapple with evil and ending in Paradiso
blocks.note: TRYING and EVIL plus O, the last letter of Paradiso, jumbled

explanation.surface: A reader struggling through Dante's great poem, from the horrors of Hell to its final heavenly book.
explanation.walkthrough: Inferno and Paradiso look like titles to admire, but they only donate letters; the question mark admits Dante's poem is really called a comedy, though it does come in three parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilogy is a set of three works, and one of divine subject in verse is a collection of poems.

clue.text: Blood count?

blocks.note: what the surface pushes: a lab test tallying cells in a blood sample
what the setter means: a nobleman, the Count, who is all about blood

explanation.surface: A nurse asking for the result of a blood test.
explanation.walkthrough: A blood count is a routine lab test; read as a nobleman with a taste for blood, the Count is Bram Stoker's vampire.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a pun: Count is Dracula's title, and blood is what the vampire feeds on.

clue.text: Victor, denied entrance, opens wide and inhales a cloud of nicotine

indicators.note: The entrance of a word is its first letter; denying it takes that letter away.

blocks.note: V is Victor in the phonetic alphabet
GAPES without its first letter G

explanation.surface: A man called Victor, turned away at the door, stands outside gaping and puffing on an e-cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor looks like a person's name; it is the radio code for V, which takes the place of the G of GAPES.
explanation.definitionFit: To vape is to breathe in nicotine vapour from an electronic cigarette.

clue.text: More likely to inquire about one that’s less quiet

indicators.note: Surrounding something is being about it.

blocks.note: someone nosier pries more
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether the one making more noise is also the more inquisitive.
explanation.walkthrough: About looks like it means concerning; here it wraps NOSIER around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain comparative synonym: making more noise is the same as being less quiet.

clue.text: You get at least 66 points playing a quiz here

definitions.text: You get at least 66 points playing a quiz here

blocks.clueFragment: You get at least 66 points playing a quiz
blocks.note: what the surface pushes: a team scoring well at a quiz night
what the setter means: laying the tiles A, Q, U, I, Z on a Scrabble board, worth 23 before the square trebles them

explanation.surface: A pub quiz where a good team can rack up plenty of points.
explanation.walkthrough: The quiz is not a trivia night: in Scrabble the tiles of QUIZ and A are worth 23, and laid on a triple-word square that becomes 69.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple-word score is the Scrabble square that trebles the value of the word played across it.

clue.text: Yorkshireman’s ultimately mean

indicators.note: Said the Yorkshire way, 'the' is clipped to a bare t', so the HE of THE is dropped.

blocks.note: a three-word phrase meaning finally

explanation.surface: A blunt Yorkshireman who, in the end, turns out to be stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean wants to be the Yorkshire stereotype of tight-fistedness; it is the verb. Yorkshire dialect shortens the to t', so 'in the end' becomes 'in t' end'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym when followed by a verb: to mean to go and to intend to go are the same thing.

clue.text: Reconsidered when decapitated, would roses suggest this description?

definitions.text: Reconsidered when decapitated, would roses suggest this description?

indicators.note: What is reconsidered is thought through again and rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order.
Decapitating removes the head, the first letter W.

blocks.note: WOULD ROSES without its head W, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A wry question: would anyone looking at a rose really call it scentless?
explanation.walkthrough: The expected answer to the question is no, since roses are famous for their scent; that tease is the whole clue's reading, while its middle words are also the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Odourless means having no smell, a description nobody would apply to roses.

clue.text: Flipping Everyman’s installing malfunctioning radar as onboard support

indicators.note: Flipping something turns it over.
To install something is to put it inside, so YM holds the other letters.

blocks.note: the setter, Everyman, speaking of what is his
RADAR rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry setter complaining that a broken radar has been fitted on his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman's stands for the setter's own MY; flipped to YM, it takes in the scrambled RADAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is the end of a spar that supports a sail on a ship.

clue.text: Slug, source of illumination?

blocks.note: slug as a verb, to punch hard; British slang has a matching four-letter verb
something that gives out light

explanation.surface: A slug crawling towards a light.
explanation.walkthrough: Slug looks like the garden creature; it is the verb to punch, and lamp is slang for hitting someone hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To lamp someone is to hit them, and a lamp gives light.

clue.text: Dictator books senior businesspeople for help with what to say

blocks.note: Idi Amin, the Ugandan dictator
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
a company's board of directors

explanation.surface: An autocrat reserving his top executives to help him write a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Books looks like a verb meaning reserves; it is the noun, the books of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot board is a screen or card showing a presenter their lines.

clue.text: Oats and nuts, never ending: I’ll see … um, on reflection …

indicators.note: Something never ending loses its end.
A reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read in reverse.

blocks.note: I'LL without its final L
SEE without its final E
as printed

explanation.surface: A hesitant diner at breakfast, stalling over the cereal choices.
explanation.walkthrough: The hesitant ums and dots look like padding, but I'll, see and um all feed the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit.

clue.text: A laundry refitted in approx. 709 hours

indicators.note: What is refitted is put together again differently, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order.

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: A laundrette being refurbished, with the work taking about a month.
explanation.walkthrough: The oddly exact figure is the definition: a lunar day, from one sunrise on the Moon to the next, lasts about 29.5 Earth days.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunar day lasts about 29.5 days, which is about 709 hours.

clue.text: … diner order – #coffee?

blocks.note: the # symbol is called a hash in Britain
coffee is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue's breakfast, with someone tagging their order online.
explanation.walkthrough: The # sign looks like a hashtag on a post; it simply gives HASH. The leading dots carry on from the muesli clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hash brown, a fried cake of grated potato, is a standard diner breakfast order.

clue.text: Cape with cruise ship following star

blocks.note: a cape or headland
an ocean liner

explanation.surface: A ship sailing past a headland, perhaps navigating by a star.
explanation.walkthrough: Star looks like a guide for sailors; it is the headline act. The wordplay comes first here and 'following' tells you the definition follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The headliner is the star performer at the top of the bill.

clue.text: Purportedly ‘everlasting’ ringlets, manmade primarily!

indicators.note: Primarily asks for what comes first, so each word gives its first letter.

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A sceptic remarking that curls sold as permanent are artificial.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, it describes the thing: a perm is short for permanent wave, though the curls grow out.
explanation.definitionFit: A perm is a chemically set hairstyle of curls, named as if permanent.

clue.text: On the spur of the moment, a simple card game

definitions.text: On the spur of the moment

blocks.clueFragment: On the spur of the moment
blocks.note: done instantly, without planning, as an adjective
the children's game of shouting when two matching cards turn up

explanation.surface: Someone deciding on a whim to play an easy game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma looks like it hangs one phrase off the other, but each side is a complete definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap decision is made on the spur of the moment, and snap is the children's card game of matching pairs.

clue.text: Way up in the Alps?

blocks.note: what the surface pushes: 'way up' as 'very high'
what the setter means: a means of going up the mountain

explanation.surface: Looks like an exclamation about how high the Alps are, or asks for a route up them.
explanation.walkthrough: Way up sounds like 'very high'; read as a way of going up, it is the chairlift that carries skiers up the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift carries people up the mountain at Alpine resorts.

clue.text: Abstract, see? Yes

blocks.note: a précis is a summary
a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is one, in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone checking they have understood a summary, and being told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: See looks like the verb 'understand'; it is a cathedral city's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Precisely, said as a reply, means yes, exactly.

clue.text: Some sketch a plinth displaying cinematic icon

indicators.note: Some of the phrase means only part of it is used.
The words put the answer on display, visible inside them.

blocks.note: sketCH A PLINth

explanation.surface: A sculptor's sketch of a statue of a film star on its pedestal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three words, so the spaces either side of 'a' have to be ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Charlie Chaplin is one of the great icons of silent cinema.

clue.text: Extremely frilly elastic pants

indicators.note: Pants is British slang for rubbish.

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: Very fancy underwear with stretchy waistbands.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like underwear; it is the British slang adjective for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The laciest thing has the most lace, so it is extremely frilly.

clue.text: Time to put into circulation paper for those suffering

blocks.note: T is time in physics
to issue banknotes or stamps

explanation.surface: A call to publish a newspaper for people in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: Paper looks like a newspaper; it is soft paper for those suffering from a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is soft paper, handed to someone with a cold or in tears.

clue.text: Baddies at home, inhabiting country houses

indicators.note: What inhabits a house lives inside it.

blocks.note: someone at home is in
a villa is a large country house

explanation.surface: Criminals lying low in grand rural homes.
explanation.walkthrough: At home giving IN is a crossword staple: someone at home is in.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the baddies of a story or film are its villains.

clue.text: Donkey attacked by bird, noisily, in side

indicators.note: Noisily asks for the words as they are heard.

blocks.note: an ass is a donkey, and a bird attacks by pecking

explanation.surface: A donkey being pecked by a bird, noisy on one flank.
explanation.walkthrough: Side looks like the donkey's flank; it is the abstract sense, a side of a question.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the abstract sense: one side of a problem is one facet of it.

clue.text: Lead 16

blocks.note: the metal, whose Latin name plumbum gives the symbol Pb, or a weight made of it
a cross-reference to 16 Across, whose answer means exactly

explanation.walkthrough: 16 points to that answer, PRECISELY; plumb is also an adverb meaning exactly, as in 'plumb in the middle'. Lead is the metal, Latin plumbum.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumb is a lead weight on a line, and plumb means precisely.

clue.text: Regressively spoils lad getting AI initially providing support for musician

indicators.note: To regress is to go backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse.

blocks.note: the spoils of a raid
a son is a lad
as printed
first letter of providing

explanation.surface: A grumble that a boy using AI is ruining things for someone backing a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoils looks like a verb about the lad; it is a noun, the plunder LOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano stool is the seat a pianist sits on.

clue.text: Somewhat nouveau, where Iris is found

indicators.note: Somewhat means only part of the word is taken.

blocks.note: noUVEAu

explanation.surface: A gallery note on where an Art Nouveau work by an artist named Iris hangs.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital I makes Iris look like a woman's name; it is the coloured part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvea is the eye's pigmented middle layer, of which the iris is part.

clue.text: The old ready for 3d info stored digitally?

blocks.note: d was the symbol for a penny in old British money
a bit is the smallest unit of digital data

explanation.surface: Old technology ready to handle three-dimensional digital files.
explanation.walkthrough: 3d looks like three-dimensional; in pre-1971 British money d meant pennies. The ready is slang for cash, and the threepenny bit was a coin worth 3d.
explanation.definitionFit: The threepenny bit was a coin of old British money, and the ready means cash.
